Hi Martin — appreciate the clear ask. Short answers and attachments below; see inline and attached stubs.

Quick summary:
- Operator access is region-scoped for normal operations: Redwood operator accounts are restricted to named operator rosters per-customer and scoped to the customer's provisioned region (EU region in your case).
- Emergency cross-region access requires documented approval (customer-signed change request + two-person Redwood approval) and is logged to our audit pipeline (immutable append-only logs retained per SOC 2 retention policy).
- PrivateLink traffic is peered into your VPC; egress is controlled by customer route tables and our recommended ACL config (attached). Keys remain in your KMS when using customer-managed KMS; Redwood only holds transient session credentials.

Attachments (stubs):
- privatelink-acl-sample.pdf — sample ACL and diagram (network arrows, ports, recommended NACL rules).
- operator-access-matrix.csv — short CSV showing roles, scope, justification, emergency escalation flow.
- sig-answers-excerpt.xlsx — CAIQ rows 3.1-3.6 mapped to our controls for region-specific operator separation.

Inline clarifications (addressing your bullets):
> "whether access is global or region-scoped"
Region-scoped by default. We operate a per-customer operator roster and scoping policy. When a customer requests additional region access we require: 1) Customer change request, 2) Two Redwood approvers (one infra lead + one security lead), 3) Temporary access window not exceeding 72 hours (unless extended by a new change request). All sessions are recorded and audited.

> "process for emergency cross-region access"
We have an Emergency Access Runbook. High-level: (a) customer files emergency CR (email + ticket), (b) Redwood SRE triages, (c) emergency access token issued with short TTL and MFA to operator, (d) session recorded to audit log. We'll share the redacted runbook link after NDA if needed.

Next steps:
- Marissa (cc'ed) will provide the SOC 2 control map and the minimal CAIQ subset we typically hand to EU-regulated pilots.
- If useful, Martin — let's lock 11 Jun 11:00 CET (your 11:00 slot) for a 20-minute call to walk the ACL diagram. If not, we'll drop the materials in the Drive and HubSpot.

Cheers,

- sig-answers-excerpt.xlsx — short excerpt; we will upload the full SIG responses to your HubSpot record once we confirm the minimal scope.

Where we differ from a typical public cloud SaaS:
- Customer-managed KMS: when configured, customer keys never leave the customer KMS; Redwood requests short-lived encryption keys for in-memory operations only.
- Operator roster: we provide a signed operator roster PDF for the pilot (names + roles + country), and we mark roster changes with effective-dates in the onboarding sheet.
- Audit retention: audit logs retained 13 months by default (SOC 2 baseline) with enterprise options for custom retention via contract line-item.
